EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Iran's new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, issued a stark vow for "definite" revenge for his father's death, prompting a direct and severe threat from US President Trump of total destruction if any assassination attempt occurs. Concurrently, US officials delivered an ultimatum to Iran to publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz open to navigation by today (Saturday) or face "serious consequences," indicating an acute and rapidly escalating geopolitical standoff.

IRAN
Mojtaba Khamenei, the newly appointed Supreme Leader, issued a written message vowing "definite" revenge for his father's death, stating that "these criminals... will take to their graves the dream of dying peacefully in their beds" and that "free people around the world" will carry out this mission. A new official website for him (Rahbar.ir) has been launched. A significant explosion occurred near a sensitive security facility in Parchin, eastern Tehran. While Iranian authorities, including the Pakdasht Governor and Fars news agency, claimed it was a controlled demolition of old ammunition, local reports described a "horrific" sound with shaking buildings and visible smoke. CNN, citing new satellite imagery from late June and early July, reported "new activity" at several nuclear and missile sites across Iran, including repair work at US/Israeli strike sites and tunnel excavation at Parchin and Kouh Kalang. Iran's acting Defense Minister, Brig. Gen. Majid Ibn Reza, stated that defensive production was not halted during the war, and drone production capacity tripled. The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baqaee, stated Iran will not allow inspection of facilities damaged by US and Israeli attacks, asserting that UN Resolution 2231 is effectively no longer legally valid. The US is demanding Iran publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz open to navigation and commit to halting attacks on commercial vessels by today (Saturday), warning of "serious consequences" if not. Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, arrived in Muscat, Oman, for talks on the Strait of Hormuz and regional developments, with Iran publicly maintaining that the Strait is open "in the Iranian way" and the world must obey. The Iranian Fars agency, close to the Revolutionary Guard, recommended that Iran retaliate for US railway bridge attacks by striking Jebel Ali port in the UAE and Haifa port in Israel, and also target ports that are part of the IMEC (India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor). US President Trump claimed Iran requested to continue "talks" and that the US agreed, but clarified the "ceasefire has ended." However, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman and a source close to the Iranian negotiating team (Fars) denied any such request, stating no negotiations will occur until the US withdraws from its positions. The US Treasury Department imposed new sanctions on Iran, targeting Ali Ansari, identified as a financial facilitator for Mojtaba Khamenei and others, and several key Iranian exchange houses, citing Iran's attacks on commercial ships in Hormuz. Araghchi accused the US of violating Article 9 of the MoU and stated that "mutual compliance" is key. US officials expressed growing pessimism about a nuclear deal due to Iran's "hostile actions" and unwillingness to make a public statement on Hormuz.

ISRAEL
The IDF killed a Hezbollah operative near a tunnel shaft on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon in an airstrike. A suspect in a vehicle posing a threat in the buffer zone was also killed. In Gaza, the IDF killed two Hamas commanders in airstrikes this week: Khalil Jamal Khalil Manna, identified as a commander in Hamas's weapon production division (killed Wednesday in northern Gaza), and Osama Walid Deeb Muhareb, identified as a company commander in Hamas's Nuseirat Battalion (killed Thursday in northern Gaza). Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced plans for three new Israeli settlements in the northern Gaza Strip. Israeli Defense Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly seeking to avoid direct confrontation with Iran currently, despite the IDF having prepared a large-scale strike plan against Iranian infrastructure. The Shin Bet confirmed it would investigate the leak of an operation in Iran but stated the decision was made before a meeting between the Shin Bet head and Channel 14 commentator Bardugo, refuting claims of political influence.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF killed two Hamas commanders this week in airstrikes: Khalil Jamal Khalil Manna, a commander in Hamas's weapon production division, and Osama Walid Deeb Muhareb, a company commander in Hamas's Nuseirat Battalion. The UN reported that Israel's demolition campaign displaced dozens of Palestinians in the West Bank during the first ten days of July. Israeli settlers attacked the al-Huwara area of Masafer Yatta, south of al-Khalil, injuring several Palestinians including women and children. Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has prepared plans for three new Israeli settlements in the northern Gaza Strip.

LEBANON
A Hezbollah operative was killed by an Israeli airstrike near a tunnel shaft on the Ali Taher ridge. Multiple Israeli airstrikes targeted Al-Mansouri in southern Lebanon, with reports of casualties. Israeli fighter jets also struck Kfar Tebnit in southern Lebanon. Israeli forces reportedly continued to set fire to Lebanese homes in Houla, southern Lebanon. A US team was sent to Beirut to ensure the ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. A Hezbollah lawmaker stated Iran's primary demands in the US agreement included an end to Israeli military offensives in Lebanon. Lebanese President stated he will not withdraw from the decision to negotiate with Israel.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Explosions were reported in Al-Sukhna, Homs countryside, attributed by some to International Coalition airstrikes targeting a cave in Jebel Al-Dhahi. Explosions were also reported in Idlib province (Al-Fouaa and Kafraya), where foreign terrorist factions are located. The "Islamic Resistance in Iraq" issued a statement vowing to develop military and security capabilities and rejecting disarmament, despite US calls for it. They praised the funeral turnout for Ayatollah Khamenei as a "million-strong popular referendum." Fires erupted in the Sinnak area of central Baghdad, causing 5 injuries, and a fire at Dublin base near Baghdad Airport. An armed attack targeted a mourning council in Sadr City, Baghdad. The Iraqi Prime Minister directed the Foreign Ministry and Army Chief of Staff to follow up on the killing of an Iraqi fisherman, Najm Abdullah, by Kuwait, and to prevent recurrence of such incidents, following a new assault by the Kuwaiti coast guard on Iraqi fishermen. The "Islamic Resistance in Iraq" suggested that the "Coordination Committee" is no longer in existence.

GULF STATES
US President Trump spoke with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman about US-Iran negotiations and the importance of maritime security. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Muscat, Oman, for talks on the Strait of Hormuz, regional developments, and bilateral relations. Pakistani Foreign Minister discussed regional developments and de-escalation with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan, expressing deep concern over heightened tensions despite the Islamabad MoU. Jordanian and Qatari foreign ministers discussed the importance of ending escalation and returning to negotiations for the Iran-US agreement. The US has demanded Iran make a public statement by today (Saturday) clarifying the Strait of Hormuz is open and committing not to fire on commercial vessels, or face "severe consequences." The USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) aircraft carrier, along with at least 3 escort warships, is sailing in the Gulf of Oman, 250-300 km from Iran's coast. The US has temporarily halted the deployment of the USS Boxer (UDK Boxer) and 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit (MEU) due to an engine cooling system malfunction, depriving the US of a rapid response capability during the naval blockade on Iran. Iran warned the UAE that it must be held accountable for supporting US military aggression against the Islamic Republic, citing US documents reportedly rewarding Abu Dhabi for military cooperation. The US Treasury Secretary stated they will continue to isolate the Iranian regime's elite and maintain seized assets for the Iranian people, specifically sanctioning Ali Ansari.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iran's New Supreme Leader Vows Revenge:** Mojtaba Khamenei, the newly appointed Supreme Leader, issued a written statement demanding "definite" revenge for his father's death from "criminal and disgraced murderers," implying global "free people" will carry out this mission.
2.  **US Ultimatum on Strait of Hormuz:** The US has given Iran until today (Saturday) to publicly declare the Strait of Hormuz fully open to navigation and commit to halting attacks on commercial vessels, warning of "serious consequences" otherwise.
3.  **US Threatens Massive Retaliation:** US President Trump directly threatened Iran with "1,000 missiles... locked and loaded" and the "complete decimation" of all areas of Iran for a year, extensible, if any attempt is made to assassinate him.
4.  **Explosion at Parchin, Iran:** A significant explosion occurred near a sensitive security facility in Parchin, eastern Tehran. While Iranian officials claimed it was a controlled demolition, local reports indicated a strong blast, and CNN satellite imagery showed new activity, including tunnel excavation and repair work, at Parchin and other nuclear/missile sites.
5.  **New US Sanctions on Iran:** The US Treasury Department imposed new sanctions on Iran, targeting Ali Ansari, a financial facilitator linked to Mojtaba Khamenei, and several Iranian exchange houses, citing Iran's attacks on commercial ships in Hormuz.
6.  **IDF Strikes in Lebanon & Gaza:** The IDF killed a Hezbollah operative on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon and two Hamas commanders (Khalil Jamal Khalil Manna, Osama Walid Deeb Muhareb) in Gaza, continuing operations despite a ceasefire.
7.  **US Naval Presence Near Iran:** The American aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) and at least three escort warships are sailing in the Gulf of Oman, 250-300 km from the Iranian coast, amid heightened tensions.
8.  **Internal Iranian Politics on Negotiations:** While US President Trump claimed Iran requested to continue talks, Iranian officials deny this, stating no negotiations will occur until the US changes its stance, indicating an internal power struggle or propaganda.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are very high. Mojtaba Khamenei's revenge vow and Trump's direct assassination threat/retaliation warning represent an acute escalation of rhetoric. The US ultimatum on Hormuz, coupled with satellite imagery of Iranian nuclear/missile site activity, suggests a rapidly approaching flashpoint. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz (imminent confrontation over navigation), Iran's nuclear/missile sites (potential for pre-emptive strikes), Southern Lebanon (IDF continues to target Hezbollah operatives in the buffer zone), and Gaza (IDF continues to target Hamas commanders despite ceasefire). The US has a significant naval presence near Iran and is using sanctions as leverage. Iran maintains a defiant stance on Hormuz control and refuses inspections of damaged sites. Fars agency explicitly suggests striking Jebel Ali and Haifa. Israel continues targeted strikes in Lebanon and Gaza but Netanyahu is reportedly cautious about direct confrontation with Iran. Key red lines for the US include any attempt to assassinate President Trump and failure to publicly commit to free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. For Iran, US attacks on critical infrastructure and violations of the MoU are red lines. Mojtaba Khamenei's statement clearly indicates revenge for his father's death is a non-negotiable red line.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is hardline, demanding public concessions from Iran, imposing new sanctions, and explicitly threatening military action. President Trump declared the ceasefire "ended," and US officials are pessimistic about a nuclear deal. Saudi Arabia and Qatar are engaging in diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions. Oman is hosting talks between Iran and the US. Pakistan is actively mediating. France noted the EU has suffered from higher oil prices due to Hormuz tensions. Russia and China, along with Iran, declared UN Security Council Resolution 2231 on Iran's nuclear file expired, rejecting further legal authority. China announced a temporary export ban on helium due to West Asia tensions. The "Islamic Resistance in Iraq" expressed strong commitment to its weapons and resistance, rejecting disarmament. Turkey and Egypt banned an LGBTQ+ cruise ship, citing incompatible social values.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions exist regarding the Parchin explosion (controlled demolition vs. massive blast), the initiation of US-Iran talks (Iran's denial vs. Trump's claim), and Iran's stance on Strait of Hormuz incidents (US claims of Iran admitting "mistake" vs. Iran's public defiance). Unverified claims include a Chinese shipping company attacked by Iran in Hormuz, an explosion at IRGC buildings in Mazandaran, and the exact number of attendees at Khamenei's funeral (140,000 vs. tens of millions). Propaganda indicators are prominent in Iranian media's portrayal of Khamenei's funeral and Mojtaba Khamenei's revenge vow, as well as Trump's intimidating rhetoric. Reporting gaps include independent verification for Parchin details, specific evidence for Iran's alleged "admission of mistake" on shipping attacks, and detailed casualty counts for Israeli strikes in Lebanon.
